because: the plan said 'let pnpm resolve it; do not guess' and pnpm resolved 7.0.79; generateObject and the ai/test mock models both exist there, so the ^6 pin in the prose was a stale guess rather than a constraint

because: the installed posthog-node 5.49.1 ships no prompt API at all — grepped every .d.ts under its dist for 'prompt' and found zero hits, so §6.2's first branch is unavailable and its REST fallback is the only path

chose: six parallel sonnet subagents, one per module boundary, over a shared contract I wrote first (schema.ts, types.ts, pipeline-contract)
over: one agent implementing the whole plan serially
because: the plan's §4 folder layout is already a clean dependency cut — merge/capture/classify/prompt-fetch/load/migration touch disjoint files once the type contract exists — so the only real coupling was the contract, and writing that myself removed it

chose: recipe_enrichment_label's PK is (recipe_id, dimension, slug), but plan §8 has the LLM writing a row for a slug the rules already own while writeLlmEnrichment only deletes method like 'llm:%'
couldBe: the instrument is wrong — the thing that PRODUCED this number, not the thing it describes
a plain insert violates the PK and every resolves-unknown case fails the whole transaction
discriminatedBy: a load.db.test.ts case that writes a rules 'unknown' row then runs writeLlmEnrichment with an LLM row for the same (dimension, slug)

chose: seed only 6 new cuisine slugs, not the plan's 24
over: seeding all 24 cuisine rows as §3.2 reads
because: measured: recipe_vocab already carries a 32-slug upstream-aliased cuisine dimension from 1785300000000, and 18 of the plan's 24 collide exactly on slug string — re-run 'select slug from recipe_vocab where dimension = cuisine' before assuming otherwise; the plan's list is the LLM's closed ENUM, not a statement about what the table lacks

chose: a CJS-require-cache probe reported that booting the recipe-enrichment workflow loaded none of ai/zod/posthog-node, which would have been true even though steps.ts statically imported schema.ts, which imports zod at its top
couldBe: the instrument is wrong — the thing that PRODUCED this number, not the thing it describes
the boot graph really is clean
discriminatedBy: a negative control that imports zod on purpose and asks the same probe whether it noticed

chose: the instrument was wrong AND the boot graph was dirty; both are now fixed
because: the negative control reported DETECTED NOTHING while zod was demonstrably imported — the CJS require cache is never populated by a pure-ESM package, so the probe was blind and its clean result was meaningless. Rebuilt on module.registerHooks (synchronous ESM load hook): the control then reported 'detected: zod' and the real boot graph came back clean over 333 modules. Separately, the original blind probe was masking a REAL eager import — steps.ts imported LLM_ENRICHMENT_VERSION statically from llm/schema.ts, which imports zod; that import is now lazy inside the two steps that need it

chose: llm-enrich RE-DERIVES the rules labels with classify() instead of reading recipe_enrichment_label back
over: a new load.ts query returning the stored rules rows
because: the step already requires status='ok', input_hash == current fingerprint AND classifier_version == deployed CLASSIFIER_VERSION before it proceeds; classify() is pure, so under those three checks the re-derived labels ARE the stored rows. The third check is the load-bearing one and is why it was added to getLlmEnrichmentState — without it the merge would reason against labels that are not in the table

chose: migrate classifyWithLlm from generateObject to generateText + Output.object
over: keeping generateObject until its deprecation gets a removal date
waiting for a plan revision before departing from L5
because: generateObject is @deprecated in ai@7 (upstream 614599a, at 6.0.0-beta.127) and its own doc comment says to switch. Measured behaviour-preserving before committing: result.output keeps the schema's inferred type (proved by assigning it to a number and reading tsc's inferred shape back — an any would have passed silently), and a schema violation still throws NoObjectGeneratedError with .text intact (checked against the mock for prose-wrapped JSON, out-of-enum, and a flat refusal). All 13 classify tests passed across the migration with no assertion changed

chose: annotate the plan doc in place with dated [SDK-1]/[SDK-2] correction notes
over: leaving the plan untouched and recording the deviation only in the results file
because: this plan is an unmerged spec that instructs implementers to call generateObject and to pin ai@^6; a future reader following it would write deprecated code. A dated note at the header plus a marker at each of the four affected spots keeps the original text readable as what was decided then, while making the correction impossible to miss
